item.title: Kagoshima Kurobuta Black Pork — Guide
item.description: Kurobuta (‘black pig’) is Kagoshima’s most celebrated meat and one of Japan’s finest pork brands. Descended from British Berkshire pigs introduced to the region and raised to strict standards — famously often fed on sweet potato — Kagoshima kurobuta is prized for its exceptionally tender, fine-textured, juicy meat with a delicate sweetness and a firm yet melting fat, considered among the best pork in the country. It’s served in many delicious ways across Kagoshima: as a thick, crisp tonkatsu (breaded cutlet), grilled, in a warming hotpot, or as the local speciality kurobuta shabu-shabu, where wafer-thin slices are briefly swished in a hot broth until just cooked and dipped in ponzu or sesame sauce — a refined way to taste the pork’s pure flavour and melting texture.
